answer: Each agent must lock 64 GB of RAM and answer ripple latency probes across random marble offsets within a 900-nanosecond budget, sealing each access with a Blake3 hash chained to the prior proof. The verifier replays a random slice and checks every echo of the hash chain against the committed root; one missed deadline or mismatched hash fails the epoch. One honest agent runs one 64 GB node; ten fakes must provision ten separate 64 GB machines with memory buses, multiplying capital cost tenfold. Peers audit public logs and slash the bond of any agent whose proofs diverge.
